segment.description: Tumbling Creek in Polk County per the catalog: a small (11.8 sq mi drainage) Cherokee National Forest tributary in the Big Frog Mountain / Allen Gap country near the Ocoee, stocked by TWRA Region 3. Identity verified: USGS 03562300 'TUMBLING CREEK NEAR ALLEN GAP, TN' (approx 35.0017, -84.4694) and TDEC station TDECWPC-TUMBL000.9PO at 35.0190, -84.4656 (0.9 mi above the mouth, county 139, HUC-8 06020003) both sit on the Polk County creek — the stocked namesakes in Humphreys/Houston counties and in Virginia/Missouri are different waters.
segment.boundaries: Cherokee NF headwaters in the Big Frog Mountain area down past the USFS Tumbling Creek Campground to the Ocoee/Hiwassee-basin confluence; full named creek per catalog (no sub-reach boundaries documented).

coldSource.notes: Small, steep, forested Cherokee NF mountain creek (the catalog's 'gradient earns the name'); USFS operates the remote 8-site Tumbling Creek Campground on its banks near the Ocoee Whitewater Center's Tanasi trail complex. No dam or spring documentation found for the creek itself.

holdover.detail: No holdover record found — no creel data, stocking-location notes, or acceptable independent angler agreement was located for carryover of the spring-stocked rainbows.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout presence documented: zero hits for 'Tumbling' on TWRA's trout-regulations lists (no wild-trout/special/DH designation; also absent from the Trout Management Plan text per the wave-3 sweep) and no fish-community survey was located. Trout presence rests entirely on the stocking program.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TDEC grabs 0.9 miles above the mouth show August water of 20.8 degC and September water of 18.2 degC in this shaded Cherokee NF mountain creek — summer temperatures at the warmest sampled point are cool enough that carryover of its spring-stocked rainbows is plausible, though no survey documents survival.
